ImageDescription.value: The famous number 28 Lisbon tram connects Martim Moniz with Campo Ourique, and passes through the popular tourist districts of Graça, Alfama, Baixa, and Estrela. The ride along the entire 28 tram route provides one of the best tours of the capital Lisbon. The little yellow Remodelado trams date from the 1990's built with boxes from the 1930's on a frame with modern engine and equipment.

ImageDescription.value: Interlaced (Gauntlet) tram tracks on the 28 tram route, in Alfama, Lisbon

Die 28 ist die berühmte Straßenbahnlinie in Lissabon. Diese historische Straßenbahn fährt durch einige der malerischsten und ältesten Viertel der Stadt, darunter Alfama, Graça und Baixa. Die Fahrt mit der Linie 28 ist eine beliebte Touristenattraktion, da sie eine großartige Möglichkeit bietet, die engen, kurvigen Straßen und die charmante Architektur Lissabons zu erleben.

ImageDescription.value: Lisbon tram 28 in the old city. The number 28 tram route is among the longest route in Lisbon, performing a loop in the east of Baixa, Graça and Alfama before heading west to Estrela and Campo de Ourique.

One attraction in Lisbon is the "roller coaster-mode" trams speeding around the historic areas of Alfama, Baixa, Chiado, and Bairo Alto.
These cars were once imported from the US and called Elétricos. Now they are replaced by buses on most <s>non-tourist</s> lines, with a notable exception of a line to Belém using more modern, articulated trams.

ImageDescription.value: From the viewpoint Portas do Sol you can see how Alfama blends with the Douro Tagus river at rhythm of fado. And at the rhythm of fado trams move by the city full of tourists. Such is the rush that sometimes there are even tram jam. In the image, trolley 543 doing line 28 to Prazeres leaves the stop at Largo das Portas do Sol while another doing line 12 waits his turn. Serve this sweet little picture to celebrate my No. 400 on Flickr.
